cases.answer: The two articles use human data for different purposes. Parameswaran et al. (2023) report a molecular association in C9FTD/ALS patients, and LeBlanc et al. report a diagnosis made in one patient. In Parameswaran et al., immunohistochemistry and immunoblotting of postmortem frontal cortex show higher phosphorylated PKR and phosphorylated eIF2α in C9ORF72 patients than in age-matched controls. The authors read this as the PKR/eIF2α pathway being activated in patients. This is a group-level comparison of a molecular marker, and it is not used to diagnose anyone. Their own wording is cautious: 'suggest'. The levels of total eIF2α varied between patients. Patient-derived iPSC motor neurons (38-day-old) showed no difference in phosphorylated PKR or eIF2α, which the authors take to mean activation happens at a later stage of disease. LeBlanc et al. is a single-patient case report. The diagnosis of FTD-ALS was made by clinical work-up, followed by genetic testing that found a GGGGCC repeat expansion in C9orf72, and then autopsy. The report says genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis and removes diagnostic uncertainty. So in LeBlanc et al. the repeat expansion is the genetic cause and confirmation of the diagnosis. In Parameswaran et al. the downstream PKR/eIF2α phosphorylation is an association measured in tissue from patients already known to carry the expansion.

cases.ambiguity: The question does not say which human observations are meant. I took them to be the postmortem and iPSC data in Parameswaran et al. and the genetic diagnosis in the LeBlanc case report.

cases.answer: No, the conclusion is not supported. Liu et al. (2024) did not test or report improved survival or motor function with Cas13d in C9-500 BAC mice. They state that this mouse model shows no survival or motor deficits, so there was nothing to rescue. They used the mice to test whether the treatment suppresses RAN translation. AAV9-Cas13d with guide S24 or S30 was injected intracerebroventricularly at P0, and brains were analysed at 13 months. Treatment significantly reduced poly-GP and poly-GA levels and poly-GA inclusions compared with the non-targeting control. Cas13d did not change C9orf72 transcript or protein levels. It also did not change RNA foci. The efficacy shown is molecular, and the word 'proved' is also too strong.
